meta.title: Apex — Q3 2026 quarterly business review
meta.description: Quarterly business review for an elevator-monitoring company: answer first, KPI scorecard, the margin trend, a win, a firmware miss, cash, Q4 roadmap, risks and three decisions.

slides.eyebrow: Apex · Q3 2026 quarterly business review · Board only
slides.heading: Margin is up, revenue is on plan, one renewal is at risk.
slides.lead: ARR closed at $31.4M and gross margin reached 68%. A firmware fault puts the $2.6M Brightline renewal in play.
slides.notes: Say all three facts before the first chart. The board should hear the risk from us, on slide one.

slides.heading: Installs in-house lifted margin; a firmware fault hit our largest customer
slides.body:
Won: gross margin rose 3 points to 68%.
Won: 3,900 new elevators connected, 400 over plan.
Missed: firmware 4.2 took 1,800 Brightline sensors offline for 11 days.
slides.aside: Decide today: fund a firmware QA team, approve the Brightline service credit, and back the Toronto pilot.
slides.notes: If the board reads one slide, it is this one. Pause on the miss; do not rush to the fix.

slides.heading: Four of five KPIs met plan; uptime missed by 0.7 points
Gross margin climbed 9 points in four quarters
slides.lead: Source: Apex finance close, 6 October 2026. Hardware and install costs included.

slides.heading: Why margin rose, and what broke
slides.lead: One decision paid off. One release did not.

slides.heading: In-house crews cut install cost from $410 to $190 per elevator
slides.body: In March we stopped paying contractors per install. Twelve Apex crews now fit sensors during the owner's routine service visit, so there is no second trip.
slides.aside: $860K saved in Q3 on 3,900 installs. Install time fell from 3.5 hours to 1.4.

slides.heading: Firmware 4.2 took 1,800 Brightline sensors offline for 11 days
slides.left:
Staged rollout: 5% of fleet, then 25%, then all.
Rollback within 2 hours.
Uptime above 99.5%.
slides.right:
Shipped to all Brightline sites at once.
No remote rollback; crews visited 214 buildings.
Fix: staged rollout enforced in code since 9 October.
slides.notes: Own it plainly. The process failed, not one engineer. The code-level gate is the real fix.

slides.heading: Runway reaches 35 months as burn falls to $1.1M

stats.label: Runway at current burn, up from 29 in Q2

slides.heading: Q4 rebuilds trust with Brightline before the January renewal

steps.title: Nov · QA
steps.body: Firmware QA team of 4 in place

slides.heading: The Brightline renewal is now the largest risk to Q1
We ask the board for three votes this quarter
slides.notes: Take the credit vote first. It is time-bound: Brightline's board meets on 12 December.

slides.heading: Protect the renewal now, and the margin gains will hold
slides.lead: All three votes today let the QA team start on 1 November.
